articles.headline: 2026 NBA free agency: Grades for offseason signings, extensions
articles.description: We're grading the biggest free agent signings and extensions, including Jalen Duren's new five-year deal.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NBAフリーエージェンシー：オフシーズンの補強と契約延長の格付け
articles.descriptionJa: Jalen Durenの新たな5年契約を含め、主要なフリーエージェントの獲得と契約延長を評価します。
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Oct. 10: Warriors sign Podziemski to five-year extension

Brandin Podziemski terms: Five years, $110 million

Grade: B-

As I wrote recently when explaining why Podziemski is a candidate to make ESPN's NBA Rank top 100 next season, the Warriors guard is underrated because he's a jack of all trades, master of none. Podziemski is a good shooter, a good passer and a good defender, but he's not amazing at any of those skills, which means he profiles more as a quality role player than a long-term star.

An average annual salary of $22 million is a reasonable deal for that level of player, especially one in his early 20s. And advanced metrics like Podziemski even more than his surface stats or reputation suggest.

This deal also fits into the Warriors' plans for next summer. According to ESPN's Anthony Slater, Podziemski's new deal will start at $18.9 million in the first year before increasing in subsequent seasons. Given that Podziemski would have had a cap hold of $17 million if he hadn't signed an extension, this extension will shave less than $2 million off the Warriors' cap space next offseason.

However, a five-year commitment at this figure is a lot for a role player. That length for a rookie extension is more typically reserved for players with more star-level upside -- such as Amen and Ausar Thompson, and Keyonte George this summer -- so the Warriors' grade for this deal slips down a notch, compared to if it had been a four-year agreement instead.

Oct. 1: Duren signs five-year deal with Pistons

Jalen Duren terms: Five years, $200 million

Grade: B

Your opinion of Duren's new contract rests on one key question: How severely do you penalize him for one bad postseason?

At the end of the regular season, Duren seemed like a shoo-in to receive at least a $200 million deal. He was a deserving All-Star and All-NBA third-team honoree, averaging 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds. He helped lead the Pistons to 60 wins and the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference. His 69% true shooting mark was by far the best in NBA history for a player with an above-average usage rate.

And Duren even played well without Cade Cunningham, showing that the center's production was not solely a product of his point guard's brillian

articles.headline: Xabi Alonso lauds Chelsea hero Jordan Henderson after brace in Bournemouth thrashing
articles.description: Xabi Alonso admitted goalscoring was not high on his list of reasons for signing Jordan Henderson after the veteran's two-goal display against Bournemouth.
articles.headlineJa: シャビ・アロンソ、ボーンマス戦で2得点を挙げたチェルシーの英雄ジョーダン・ヘンダーソンを称賛
articles.descriptionJa: ボーンマス戦で2ゴールを挙げたベテラン、ジョーダン・ヘンダーソンについて、シャビ・アロンソは、彼を獲得した理由として得点力を最優先していたわけではないと認めました。
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso admitted goalscoring was not high on his list of reasons for signing Jordan Henderson after the veteran's two-goal display against Bournemouth.

Henderson, 36, rolled back the years with a pair of superb strikes and provided an assist for Morgan Rogers in a thumping 5-1 win.

The former Liverpool captain was brought in on a surprise free transfer from Brentford over the summer to bring some leadership to Chelsea's callow ranks.

But on the day Cole Palmer announced he had signed a new eight-year contract, the player 12 years his senior stole the show.

"We signed him for everything," said Blues boss Alonso. "If he's able to score two beauties like today we are more than happy for him.

"But apart from the goals he's done many good things. I think that today was a very complete performance."

Chelsea are the Premier League's fast starters and there were only 65 seconds on the clock when Palmer fed Henderson, who crashed a first-time shot in off a post.

Just over a minute later Henderson teed up Rogers, whose curler flicked the head of António Silva on its way into the net.

- Jordan Henderson, 36, nets unlikely brace as Chelsea thrash Bournemouth

- Brighton keep pressure on Man City, Arsenal with 2-0 Sunderland win

- Chelsea's Cole Palmer signs new contract until 2034

João Pedro got in on the act just 40 seconds into the second half, and the Brazilian doubled his tally after Evanilson had pulled one back for Bournemouth before Henderson curled in a free-kick to wrap up the scoring.

Asked about Chelsea's lightning start to games, Alonso said: "I have nothing to do with it, so I don't have the answer.

"We always speak about how we try to start the game well and give good energy, but I have no explanation, no credit to me.

"It has never happened to me in such a short period to score that many early goals, so let's see if we can keep doing that.

"But after the goals, many other things need to happen. Maybe, I'd prefer to score the first one in the last minute. It will happen one day, hopefully."

Bournemouth had lost only once in their previous 13 trips to London, but they were pulverised in the October sunshine and are still winless after six matches under new head coach Marco Rose.

"We played not good, so a deserved loss, especially the way we started both halves," said the German.

"We know Chelsea is a team that starts well and it is our responsibility that we didn't act in the right way. It's my responsibility, and we have to do better. We struggled for long periods in the game.

"We need to stick together, we knew it would be a demanding season."

articles.headline: Premier League live updates: Man United host Tottenham in game of the day
articles.description: After a three-week international break, club soccer returns! Man United host a Tottenham side bottom of the table and still searching for their first league win.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ速報：本日の注目の一戦、マン・Uがトッテナムをホームに迎える
articles.descriptionJa: 3週間の代表ウィークを経て、クラブサッカーが復活！マン・Uは、リーグ最下位で今季初勝利を模索するトッテナムをホームに迎えます。
articles.body:
After a three-week international break, European club soccer returns this weekend!

Saturday in the Premier League began with defending champions Arsenal having to come from behind to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium. Then it was over to Chelsea, who scored two goals in the opening three minutes against Bournemouth on their way to an emphatic 5-1 home win.

Our match of the day saw two teams desperate to turn their seasons around, as Manchester United hosted a Tottenham Hotspur side who were bottom of the table and still searching for their first league win of the season. They didn't find it at Old Trafford, where they largely outplayed their hosts, went behind, but fought back to earn a 1-1 draw.

There's plenty of action across the continent, too. Bayern Munich conceded the quickest goal ever scored in the Bundesliga in their 2-2 draw at Augsburg. In LaLiga, Alavés fell to 2-1 Atlético Madrid, while champions Barcelona host Getafe. Meanwhile, Inter Milan cruised to a 3-0 win over Parma in Serie A.

Enjoy all the updates from Saturday's matches.

articles.headline: Colts place DE Arden Key on IR with hamstring injury
articles.description: Colts defensive end Arden Key has been placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, meaning he will miss at least four games before returning to the active roster.
articles.headlineJa: コルツ、DEアーデン・キーをハムストリングの負傷によりIRへ
articles.descriptionJa: コルツのディフェンシブエンド、アーデン・キーがハムストリングの負傷により負傷者リスト（IR）入りしました。これにより、アクティブ・ロースターに戻るまで少なくとも4試合を欠場することになります。
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts defensive end Arden Key was placed on injured reserve Saturday with a hamstring injury, meaning he will miss at least four games before returning to the active roster.

Key sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Washington Commanders, prompting the Colts to seek solutions to the hole left in their defensive lineup. Key has played 64% of the Colts' defensive snaps this season.

The Colts signed veteran free agent Carl Lawson to their practice squad this week to add depth, but Lawson was not activated Saturday. Instead, the absence of Key will mean a bigger role for second-year player Jaylahn Tuimoloau and, possibly, rookie George Gumbs Jr.

Also Saturday, the Colts ruled out veteran wide receiver Darius Slayton for their Week 5 game at the Pittsburgh Steelers after he sustained a knee injury in Friday's practice. Slayton was possibly in line to make his debut after signing with the Colts last month. To address the position, Indianapolis promoted Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from the practice squad.

articles.headline: Sources: Cardinals finalizing deal to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr.
articles.description: The Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade Marvin Harrison Jr., sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.headlineJa: 関係筋：カージナルス、WRマービン・ハリソン・Jr.のトレード交渉を最終調整中
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNのアダム・シェフター記者とNFLネットワークのイアン・ラポート記者によると、カージナルスはマービン・ハリソン・Jr.をトレードする契約を最終段階に進めている。
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- The Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Saturday.

The Cardinals informed Harrison that he will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions as the trade is completed, sources said.

One team that has had talks with Arizona is Houston, which has been, and is thought to be, squarely in the mix for Harrison, sources told Schefter and Rapoport. If Harrison is traded to the Texans, he would be reunited with his college quarterback C.J. Stroud.

The Indianapolis Colts are not involved in talks for Harrison, a source told ESPN's Stephen Holder. The Cardinals were asking for a second-round choice and more, according to a source, for the son of Marvin Harrison Sr., the Hall of Famer who owns multiple Indianapolis receiving records.

Marvin Harrison Jr. has been the center of trade speculation for weeks as he got off to a slower-than-expected start to the season. He had just one catch in the first two games, fueling chatter that his time in Arizona could be coming to an end this season, short of his rookie contract ending.

Harrison has five catches on 12 targets for 85 yards and a touchdown through four games this season as the fifth-most-targeted player on the Cardinals offense. Tight end Trey McBride, wide receivers Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne, and running back Jeremiyah Love all have more targets than Harrison, who was tied with the sixth-most receptions.

Harrison's only touchdown of the season came in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. After the touchdown, while sitting on the turf, Harrison raised his right index finger to the mouth area of his face mask to indicate a "shush" motion. Asked Thursday about what message he wanted to get across with the celebration, Harrison said: "No message."

He said this week that he hasn't paid attention to the trade speculation. But on Sept. 23, Harrison hired Todd France and Tory Dandy as his agents, according to the NFLPA online database. Harrison did not have an agent prior to then.

The No. 4 pick in the 2024 draft, Harrison had 1,578 receiving yards and 13 touchdown catches in 33 games with the Cardinals. He hasn't reached 1,000 yards in a season and dealt with foot injuries and appendicitis last season that led to him playing in just 12 games in which he caught 41 passes for 608 yards and four touchdowns.

As a rookie, Harrison had 885 receiving yards and eight touchdowns on 62 catches.

After Sunday's loss, coach Mike LaFleur said he still has faith in Harrison.

"Yeah, my confidence is high in Marv," LaFleur said.

Entering the weekend, Arizona told teams that it was looking for first-round value for Harrison, yet other teams have viewed him as worthy of some form of second-day pick compensation, sources said.

Sources said Harrison hired France and Dandy to try to navigate a potential trade, and the interest has been significant

articles.headline: Riccardo Calafiori channels David Beckham with Arsenal goal in England vs. Greece anniversary boots
articles.description: Arsenal's Riccardo Calafiori can lay claim to a unique first after his goal against Leeds United at the Emirates on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: リッカルド・カラフィオーリ、イングランド対ギリシャ戦記念モデルのスパイクでゴール、ベッカムを彷彿
articles.descriptionJa: アーセナルのリッカルド・カラフィオーリは、土曜日にエミレーツで行われたリーズ・ユナイテッド戦でのゴールにより、独自の快挙を成し遂げた。
articles.body:
Arsenal's Riccardo Calafiori can lay claim to a unique first after his goal against Leeds United at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday. 

Calafiori scored Arsenal's initial equaliser after James Justin opened the scoring for Leeds, and he did so wearing the special edition David Beckham predators, made to celebrate 25 years since his free-kick against Greece that took England to the 2002 World Cup. 

And so, the Italian became not only the first professional player to wear them but also the first to score with them on. 

Bruno Guimarães scored Arsenal's second of the afternoon as they came back from a goal down to get back to winning ways after the extended international break. 

The boots, made by Adidas, was co-designed by Beckham himself and is "inspired by one of the most defining moments in both David Beckham's career and Predator history," according to the company. 

"Few moments in football history capture the spirit of Predator quite like David Beckham's free kick against Greece," Sam Handy, General Manager of Adidas Football said.

"With this special edition release, we wanted to honour that moment through a design that combines authentic football heritage, premium craftsmanship and modern performance innovation."

- Arsenal fight back to win as Premier League resumes under cloud of Man City verdict

articles.headline: '51 years': Man United fans revive Man City 'trophy drought' banner after financial charges verdict
articles.description: Manchester United fans reset the clock on their Stretford End 'ticker' on Saturday to make clear their views on how Manchester City should be punished for breaching the Premier League's financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: 「51年」：財務規定違反の裁定を受け、マンUファンがマンCの「無冠の期間」バナーを復活
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのファンは土曜日、ストレトフォード・エンドにある「タイマー」をリセットし、プレミアリーグの財務規定違反に対するマンチェスター・シティへの罰則についての見解を明らかにした。
articles.body:
Manchester United fans reset the clock on their Stretford End 'ticker' on Saturday to make clear their views on how Manchester City should be punished for breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

The banner first appeared back in 2000, showing it was '24 years' since Manchester City had won their last major trophy, the 1976 League Cup.

It was updated each season, reaching '35 years' before City ended their trophy drought by lifting the FA Cup in 2011, when the banner was taken down.

But after it was announced two weeks ago that City had been found guilty of almost all of the charges relating to breaches of financial regulations between 2009 and 2018, the banner reappeared ahead of Saturday's match against Tottenham, paid for the by The Red Army supporters group.

Now updated to read '51 years', the supporters have made clear they do not feel any of the 22 major honours City have won under the ownership of the Abu Dhabi United Group are legitimate.

There were also chants of 'You cheating b------s, you know what you are' before kick-off.

No punishment has yet been announced for City, who have appealed against the verdict of the independent commission and stated that the verdict "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

Michael Carrick, meanwhile, said before the Tottenham game that being awarded medals retrospectively as a consequence of Manchester City's financial rule breaking will not replace the winning "moments" he was denied.

Carrick was a player under Sir Alex Ferguson when United came second in the Premier League behind City in 2012 and also when Jose Mourinho's team finished runners-up to City in 2018.

- 'We're Not Really Here': As Man City sanctions loom, it's the fans who suffer

- City whistleblower to remain in witness protection

- Arteta insists conscience is clear over time at Man City

Both seasons fall within the Premier League's investigation into City's finances between 2009 and 2018.

"It's the moment that you strive for -- to win and achieve in that moment -- so the medal here or there, not getting blasé about it, but that doesn't bring the feeling of when you initially win or you don't win," he said. "That's essentially what we're all in it for."

Information from PA and ESPN's Rob Dawson was used in this report.

articles.headline: Manuel Neuer error sees Robin Fellhauer score fastest-ever Bundesliga goal
articles.description: Augsburg's Robin Fellhauer wrote his name into German soccer history Saturday, scoring the fastest goal in Bundesliga history against Bayern Munich.
articles.headlineJa: マヌエル・ノイアーのミスでロビン・フェルハウアーがブンデス史上最速ゴールを記録
articles.descriptionJa: アウクスブルクのロビン・フェルハウアーは土曜日、バイエルン・ミュンヘン戦でブンデスリーガ史上最速のゴールを決め、ドイツサッカーの歴史にその名を刻んだ。
articles.body:
Augsburg's Robin Fellhauer wrote his name into German soccer history Saturday, scoring the fastest-ever Bundesliga goal in a draw against Bayern Munich courtesy of a comical Manuel Neuer error. 

It took Fellhauer just eight seconds to latch onto a loose pass from Neuer before tucking home into an empty net almost immediately after Bayern had kicked off. 

Neuer received the ball from the center circle in what was the first pass of the game, before taking a touch and attempting to lift it over the midfielder, but Fellhauer took it off his toes and around the German keeper to put Augsburg in front in record time. 

But it was a lead that Augsburg couldn't hold onto, with Ismael Saibari equalizing for the visitors after the break.

Rodrigo Ribeiro then tapped home to put Augsburg a goal to the good once again, before Nathaniel Brown salvaged a late point for Bayern. It was, though, a result that saw them drop off the top of the Bundesliga table while Augsburg moved into fifth. 

Earliest goals in Bundesliga history

Robin Fellhauer: 8 seconds vs. Bayern Munich

Kevin Volland: 9 seconds vs. Bayern Munich 

Karim Bellarabi: 9 seconds vs. Bayer Leverkusen

Ulf Kirsten: 11 seconds vs. FC Kaiserslautern

Giovane Elber: 11 seconds vs. Hamburger SV

Information from ESPN Global Research contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Warriors give Brandin Podziemski 5-year, $110M extension
articles.description: Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski has agreed to a five-year, $110 million extension, his agent told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.headlineJa: ウォリアーズ、ブランディン・ポジェムスキーと5年1億1000万ドルの契約延長に合意
articles.descriptionJa: ウォリアーズのガード、ブランディン・ポジェムスキーは5年総額1億1000万ドルの契約延長に合意したと、彼の代理人がESPNのシャムス・チャラニア記者に語った。
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors and starting guard Brandin Podziemski have agreed to a five-year, $110 million contract extension, his agent Bill Duffy told ESPN's Shams Charania, avoiding restricted free agency next summer.

The fully guaranteed deal includes a mutual option in the final season (2031-32) and a trade kicker. The unique mutual option allows either side to opt in, but not opt out, of the final season of the deal, allowing both sides to reopen potential extension conversations that offseason.

Podziemski, 23, is entering his fourth season after the Warriors selected him 19th overall in the 2023 NBA draft. He was the first pick of general manager Mike Dunleavy's tenure and a player Dunleavy and the front office prioritized keeping in the fold.

He will make $5.6 million this season in the final year of his rookie deal. That figure will jump up to $18.9 million next season in the first year of the extension.

As contract talks intensified in the past month, keeping that initial salary number at a manageable level was an important negotiation point on the Warriors' side, team sources said.

Dunleavy has been protective of the team's 2027-28 cap space, building a roster loaded with expiring contracts while convincing superstar guard Stephen Curry that the benefit of taking a $10 million pay cut for next season is in maintaining the ability to better transform the roster around him via free agency or trade in his final seasons. The Warriors have four tradable first-round picks.

Podziemski had a projected cap hold next summer of around $17 million, so his first-year salary will slice an extra $1.9 million from what could have been available had they pushed the conversation to restricted free agency.

The Warriors could still have somewhere between $55 million to $60 million in space, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks, considering they can cut veteran center Kristaps Porzingis, who has only $3 million of his $20 million for next season guaranteed and is out indefinitely with a health issue.

Expectations are relatively low for the Warriors entering the regular season. They are without starting wings Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody (both are rehabbing serious knee injuries), and it remains unclear when they will get Porzingis back, keeping them without three of their top six players.

But Podziemski's presence has become a constant. He was one of only 18 NBA players to appear in all 82 games last season, setting career highs in points per game (13.8), made 3s, assists and steals.

His youth and durability are valued on a roster that is otherwise aging and incessantly banged up. Warriors coach Steve Kerr calls Podziemski a "connector" and points to his underlying metrics as a sign of his positive contributions.

Podziemski is an elite rebounder at the guard position, averaging more than five per game in all three of his seasons while ranking in the top three in charges drawn since he has entered the NBA.

"Brandin is a huge part of our team," Kerr

articles.headline: Can the Seahawks' defense again silence the 49ers' hot offense Sunday?
articles.description: Seattle's defense stole the show the past two times these teams met. But the 49ers and Brock Purdy are on a roll heading into Week 5.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスの守備は、日曜日に再び好調な49ersの攻撃を封じ込められるか？
articles.descriptionJa: 前回までの2度の対戦では、シアトルの守備が主役となった。しかし、49ersとブロック・パーディは第5週に向けて勢いに乗っている。
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- It took Mike Macdonald several weeks to rewatch the Seattle Seahawks' 29-13 victory in Super Bowl LX. It was partly because of his packed schedule and partly because of his perfectionist ways. The head coach and defensive playcaller knew that even though his unit had dominated the New England Patriots, it had also made miscues that would eat at him once he saw them on film.

Macdonald had no such hang-ups about either of Seattle's two January victories over the San Francisco 49ers, a pair of defensive masterpieces in which the Seahawks held their divisional rivals out of the end zone -- first in Week 18, then again in the divisional round of the playoffs.

That was then.

The 49ers (4-0) and their offense are rolling heading into an NFC West clash with the Seahawks (3-1) on Sunday at Lumen Field. San Francisco ranks second in points per game (30.5), Brock Purdy leads the league in Total QBR (89.2), and the quarterback has a few playmakers who weren't on the team nine months ago.

"None of what happened last year matters," Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones IV said. "It's a new year, new season. They've got a hell of a group. They've put together four good games, won every one of them. Just like we have a new team, they've got a new team. They're doing some different things. We've just got to go out there and do our job."

In the first of two defensive performances that even Macdonald might have considered perfect, the Seahawks held Kyle Shanahan's team to 173 total yards in last year's regular-season finale, a winner-take-all affair in which the NFC West and No. 1 seed were on the line. Seattle intercepted one of Purdy's passes, forced two more turnovers on downs and limited Christian McCaffrey to 23 yards on eight carries in a 13-3 victory at Levi's Stadium.

When the Seahawks hosted the 49ers after their first-round bye, it was more of the same. Macdonald's top-ranked scoring defense allowed only 236 yards, generated three takeaways to go along with three more turnovers on downs, and bottled up McCaffrey again (35 rushing yards on 11 attempts) in a 41-6 rout.

While appearing on NBC's pregame coverage of Super Bowl LX, Shanahan said self-deprecatingly that his "expert opinion" on the Seahawks might not be worth much given that his offense couldn't generate a touchdown against them during the past two times they met.

"We tackled really well. We limited extra yardage. I thought we rushed the quarterback with discipline and married the coverage," Macdonald recalled this week. "That's what it takes to play really good football, in general. But the guys played hard, played physical, played well situationally."

Said safety Julian Love: "I think we communicated really well. I think these guys do a lot of stuff pre-snap, motions, shifts, crazy alignment-type things. articles.body:
Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Buccaneers defeated the Cowboys on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 14 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Giants pull off an upset? How many yards will Steelers running back Jaylen Warren record against the Colts? Is Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett a safe starter in fantasy? And which Bears receiver will find the end zone? Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Las Vegas Raiders +3.5 (+164 moneyline) at New England Patriots

Patriots QB Drake Maye's breakout against the Bills last week didn't solve New England's protection problems. He was still heavily pressured, while his receivers didn't create much yardage after the catch.

Meanwhile, Raiders QB Kirk Cousins has a useful answer against this defense: play-action. New England is much tougher when quarterbacks simply drop back, but it has allowed the fifth-highest QBR against play-action this season. That fits what Cousins does best, giving Las Vegas a way to manufacture enough offense to create tension.

New York Giants +3.5 (+150 moneyline) at Washington Commanders

Giants QB Jameis Winston showed against the Cardinals last week that he can find WR Malik Nabers and produce touchdowns. That ability, combined with the Commanders' poor pass defense, is what makes this a live play Sunday. Washington's blitz-happy approach only helps if it disrupts Winston before he finds those openings.

Offensively, the Commanders will return QB Jayden Daniels, but they've struggled to stay out of third-and-long. The Giants' secondary has limited passing yardage while creating interceptions this season (six, tied for the most in the NFL).

Walder predicts three stat lines

Jaylen Warren, RB, Pittsburgh Steelers: 16 carries, 104 yards, 1 touchdown, 1 reception, 19 receiving yards

Warren has been getting a heavy workload this season, and there's no reason that shouldn't continue Sunday against the Colts. Indy ranks 30th in run stop win rate and 25th in opponent EPA per designed carry. It has surrendered 4.8 yards per carry (tied for fifth most), and that number holds steady against duo runs, which the Steelers run frequently (33% of the time).

I do expect Warren's production will be more on the ground in this game than usual, however, because the Colts play a lot of man coverage, which usually discourages RB targets and receptions.
